concepts.title: Matter Is Made of Particles
concepts.definition: All matter is built from tiny particles far too small to see; dissolving a spoon of salt in water or smelling food from another room shows that substances break into minute pieces that spread through liquids and air.
concepts.key_idea: Dissolving and spreading smells are everyday proofs that matter is particulate.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu107.txt lines 40-168 (what is matter composed of)
question_patterns: what evidence shows that matter is made of tiny particles
why does salt disappear when dissolved in water
how does the smell of food reach us from a distance
why can particles of matter not be seen with the naked eye
explain the particulate nature of matter with an activity
what happens to a crystal of potassium permanganate in water

solution_steps.explain: Salt or crystals vanish into water yet colour or taste the whole liquid - they have broken into invisible particles.
Smells travel because particles mix into the air and move freely.
All matter consists of minute particles with spaces between them.

concepts.title: States of Matter and Interparticle Space
concepts.definition: Whether matter is solid, liquid or gas depends on how far its particles sit and how strongly they cling: solids pack particles tightly in fixed positions, liquids keep them close but mobile, and gases spread them far apart with almost no attraction.
concepts.key_idea: Spacing and attraction decide the state: tight-fixed, close-mobile, or far-free.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu107.txt lines 168-452 (what decides different states of matter)
question_patterns: compare the interparticle spacing in solids, liquids and gases
why do solids have a fixed shape while gases do not
what decides the state of a substance
why can gases be compressed easily but not solids
arrange solids, liquids and gases by increasing interparticle attraction
explain the properties of the three states using the particle idea

solution_steps.explain: Solid particles touch in fixed spots, liquid particles stay near but slide, gas particles fly far apart.
Strong attraction holds shape; weak attraction lets flow and escape.
Fixed shape, flowing liquid and compressible gas all follow from the particle picture.

concepts.title: Change of State by Heating and Cooling
concepts.definition: Heating pushes particles apart and faster, turning solids into liquids and liquids into gases; cooling reverses the journey - melting, boiling, condensation and freezing are just particles gaining or losing energy and space.
concepts.key_idea: Add energy to loosen the particle crowd, remove it to let them settle.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu107.txt lines 452-591 (how does interparticle spacing change)
question_patterns: what happens to particles when ice melts
explain boiling using the particle idea
how does condensation change the spacing of particles
name the changes of state with one example each
why does heating increase interparticle spacing
how does cooling a gas turn it into liquid

solution_steps.explain: Particles gain energy, vibrate more and widen their spacing: solid becomes liquid, then gas.
Losing energy slows particles and draws them close: gas condenses, liquid freezes.
Melting, boiling, condensation and freezing label the four paths.

concepts.title: Movement of Particles in Different States
concepts.definition: Particle motion differs by state: solid particles only vibrate about fixed spots, liquid particles slide past one another, and gas particles dart freely in all directions - which is why gases spread fastest and mix by diffusion.
concepts.key_idea: Vibrate, slide, fly - the three motion styles explain diffusion and flow.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu107.txt lines 591-680 (how particles move in different states)
question_patterns: how do particles move in solids, liquids and gases
what is diffusion and in which state is it fastest
why do solid particles only vibrate
compare the motion of particles in water and in steam
why does the smell of incense spread through the whole room
which state of matter shows the maximum particle motion

solution_steps.explain: Vibration in solids, gliding in liquids, free flight in gases.
Freely flying gas particles mix fastest - diffusion is quickest in gases.
Higher temperature speeds the motion in every state.
